text:
mia: Heads up — trying to run the Ruby quickstart on a fresh Windows 11 VM with Ruby 3.2 and getting a weird Bundler error: it can't find the Gemfile even though I'm in the sampleapp dir. Anyone seen this?

sam: Huh. Do you have WSL or native Ruby? Windows + native Ruby can be quirky with binstubs/gem paths.

mia: Native (installed via RubyInstaller). Repro steps: unzip sampleapp, cd sampleapp, `bundle install` -> error: 
```
Could not locate Gemfile
```
But `ls` shows Gemfile is there.

devrel_alejandra: Oof. Two immediate things: 1) sometimes CRLF vs LF makes windows console weirdly interpret filenames, 2) bundler lookup can choke if running from a symlinked path or if `BUNDLE_GEMFILE` env var is set. Can you run `ruby -v && bundle -v && echo %BUNDLE_GEMFILE%` in cmd, or `$env:BUNDLE_GEMFILE` in PowerShell?

mia: Ran those: `ruby 3.2.2p0`, `Bundler version 2.4.10`, and `%BUNDLE_GEMFILE%` is empty. I also noticed the sample app has a top-level `scripts/setup.sh` that assumes `bash`, and my Windows shell ignored it.

sam: Okay that tracks. Quick fix: run within `bash` (Git Bash) or WSL, or create a tiny `bin/setup` Windows-friendly script. Alternatively, you can explicitly point bundler: `BUNDLE_GEMFILE=./Gemfile bundle install` (PowerShell: `$env:BUNDLE_GEMFILE='./Gemfile'; bundle install`).

mia: Try that now... interesting, setting `BUNDLE_GEMFILE` made bundler see it. But I still hit a require error when starting the sample: `LoadError: cannot load such file -- redwood` even after `bundle install`.

harry: That suggests the quickstart's `Gemfile` uses a path gem or local gemspec reference that isn't built/installed on Windows. Which line in Gemfile references the SDK?

mia: Gemfile has `gem 'redwood', path: '../ruby-sdk'` because the repo includes both SDK and sampleapp. On Windows that relative path resolution can break if the unpacked folder has spaces or the path length hits 260 chars.

devrel_alejandra: Good catch. Two small improvements we should make: 1) update quickstart README to note Windows caveats and recommend WSL/Git Bash, 2) add a `gem 'redwood'` fallback (published gem) in Gemfile for people who just want to run the sample without the monorepo layout. I'll open a PR.

sam: Another idea: include a tiny `bin/setup` that does `bundle config set --local path 'vendor/bundle' && bundle install` and also a `bin/windows-setup.ps1` with `$env:BUNDLE_GEMFILE='./Gemfile'; bundle install`. That should reduce friction.

mia: That would be amazing. Also noticed our README shows `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` which confused our QA (PowerShell uses `$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = '...'`). Could we add both bash and PowerShell snippets?

devrel_alejandra: Absolutely. I'll add both and a short note: "If you're on native Windows, prefer PowerShell/Git Bash, or use WSL for full parity". 

harry: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 — updates README, adds bin/setup and windows script, and switches Gemfile to try local path then fallback to rubygems if present. CI run queued.

ci-bot: CI: Build for PR #412 started. :gear:

mia: Tested PR changes locally (ran `bin/windows-setup.ps1` in admin PowerShell) — works 🎉. Thanks y'all. Can we also add a tiny note about long path support (enable via registry or `Enable-LongPaths`) to avoid `LoadError` on very deep paths?

devrel_alejandra: Good call, will add short troubleshooting section for path length and CRLF issues. I'll merge once CI green and one more reviewer approves. :thumbsup:
